Environmental performance of the newer composite materials, such as fiber-reinforced plastics, is being carefully monitored to control their performance when exposed to fire.
b) New Production Methods: All of the selected BREAKTHROUGH housing systems utilize factory production for a portion of the product, and some involve almost the complete assembly of the housing unit in the factory. Each of the system producers was required to submit for HUD review and approval his production plans and quality control program.
c) Transportation: Factory production of housing or housing elements implies transportation of this housing to its destination. Highway shipment has been the traditional method of transportation, and HUD has worked closely with the Interstate Commerce Commission and with the Department of Transportation in questions of tariffs, truck sizes and similar factors. At the same time, efforts are under way with the railroad industry to develop equipment and procedures to permit modular shipment by rail over extended distances. Where highway shipment is limited to approximately 250-400 miles, rail shipments of three times this distance are possible, with less potential problem of damage enroute. The concept of rail shipment has been tested in BREAKTHROUGH by two "unit trains" of housing from Battle Creek, Michigan, to the King County, Washington, site and by several carloads of modules from Chester, Pennsylvania, to the Memphis, Tennessee, site.
d) <u>Design Considerations</u>: Design of the BREAKTHROUGH systems continues to represent an attempt to produce conventional housing forms despite changes in materials, production methods and other factors. For a housing system to be successful in the marketplace, it must provide an attractive alternate to conventional housing; technology, price and faster delivery alone will not fill this need. The BREAKTHROUGH designs have been closely monitored to encourage good design, and spatial characteristics have been controlled by criteria now being adapted for implementation through the Minimum Property Standards program.
e) <u>Housing Types</u>: BREAKTHROUGH involves four different "types" of housing: multi-family high rise, multi-family low rise (not requiring an elevator), single-family attached (such as a town- or row-house), and single-family detached. In accordance with HUD policy, high rise buildings are with few exceptions limited to two-bedroom units or smaller, to serve small families or elderly individuals. Wherever possible, units for large families have direct access to the ground level.
f) Standards for Evaluation: It was noted earlier that performance standards were developed by NBS to provide the basis for the design and evaluation of the various elements of the housing system.
